# ARCHITECTURE.md — Saans v1 system architecture

**Status:** v1 design, 17 Nov 2026 (Phase 4). Built from DECISIONS D-011 to D-028.
**Image:** `saans_architecture_v1.png` / `.svg` (generated by `build_arch.py`; goes into the repo's `docs/` in Phase 7).
**Mayank's hand-built copy:** Miro board "Saans v1 Architecture" (D-009). Review status at the bottom.

---

## 1. The system in one paragraph
Every hour an **external cron** starts a **GitHub Actions** job.
1. The job pulls fresh station data (OpenAQ, or CPCB when reachable), the **pinned GFS weather forecast**, the latest **CAMS** run and **satellite fires**.
2. It validates them, builds **only features that were knowable at issue time** (with the real data delay simulated), and runs the **champion LightGBM model** to get calibrated p10/p50/p90 forecasts for every station for 72 hours.
3. It explains each forecast with **SHAP driver families** and publishes a few small JSON files to a **Hugging Face dataset**.
4. It then tells the **Vercel** website to refresh.

Visitors get cached pages from the edge in under 2.5 s. When they chat, a **grounded agent** reads the same JSON through read-only tools, and a **number validator** blocks any number not found in those tools. Nightly jobs score yesterday's forecasts for the public scoreboard; weekly jobs retrain and promote a new model only if it passes the gate.

## 2. Zones and components
| Zone | Component | Job | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Data sources | CPCB Data Repository | 15-min history; one-time backfill from the laptop (Indian IP) | D-011 |
| | OpenAQ v3 | Live observations for cloud jobs (≈ 2 h 50 min delay) | D-011, D-028 |
| | Open-Meteo GFS (pinned) | Weather forecast live + archive (as issued) | D-012, D-027 |
| | Copernicus ADS (CAMS) | As-issued CAMS by lead time → training + baseline | D-013 |
| | Open-Meteo CAMS live | Latest CAMS run for live serving; parity-checked vs ADS | D-013 |
| | NASA FIRMS | Fires from NOAA-20/21 + MODIS (no S-NPP) | D-015 |
| | City config (YAML) | Stations, OpenAQ↔CPCB crosswalk, calendar, delays, pinned model | D-025 |
| 2 Pipeline | cron-job.org → GitHub Actions | Reliable hourly trigger; free 4-vCPU runners | D-020 |
| | hourly.yml | Ingest → Validate → Features → Forecast → Explain → Publish | D-016, D-021 |
| | nightly.yml | Evaluate → Scoreboard → Drift report | D-022 |
| | weekly.yml | Train (champion vs challenger) → Promotion gate → Register | D-021, D-022 |
| | ci.yml + Monitoring | Tests, parity checks, agent eval; status.json and banners | D-026 |
| 3 Storage (HF Hub) | `<name>-data` | Parquet lake: raw / clean / features / forecast_archive | D-019 |
| | `<name>-live` | `latest/*.json`, the only thing the website and agent read | D-016, D-019 |
| | `<name>-models` | Model versions, metrics, CHAMPION pointer, model card | D-022 |
| 4 Serving (Vercel) | Web pages (ISR) | Map, station, scoreboard, about; edge-cached | D-023 |
| | /api/revalidate | Pipeline-triggered refresh | D-023 |
| | /api/chat | Grounded agent with read-only tools + number validator | D-008, D-024 |
| | Upstash Redis | Rate limit + answer cache | D-024 |
| | LLM fallback chain | Groq → Gemini → OpenRouter | D-024 |
| 5 Users | Browser / mobile | The five personas (D-004) | D-004 |
| | OpenFreeMap | Map tiles straight to the browser, no key | D-023 |

## 3. Numbered flows (same numbers as on the diagram)
1. cron-job.org triggers the hourly workflow (`workflow_dispatch`).
2. Ingest pulls every source (fallback chain, every row tagged with its source).
3. The pipeline reads and writes the lake (raw, clean, features, forecast archive).
4. Forecast loads the CHAMPION model.
5. The weekly Register step writes a new model version, only if it passed the gate.
6. Publish writes `latest/*.json` to `<name>-live`.
7. The pipeline calls `/api/revalidate`, so pages refresh within seconds.
8. Pages read `latest/*.json` (cached at the edge until the next revalidate).
9. Agent tools read the same `latest/*.json` (one source of truth).
10. Agent ↔ Redis (rate limit, cache) and ↔ the LLM chain (fallback).
11. Users load pages.
12. Users chat with the agent.

## 4. Why this shape (one line each, for interviews)
- **Batch + CDN, not a model server:** inputs change hourly, so per-request inference only adds cost and cold starts (D-016).
- **One JSON source of truth for pages *and* agent:** the agent cannot disagree with the page, and the validator can check every number against it (D-008).
- **Three leakage guards built into Features:** as-issued weather (D-012), as-issued CAMS (D-013), real data delay (D-028).
- **Failure is visible, not silent:** status.json, data-age labels, a "data delayed" banner, failure emails (D-026).
- **Swappable parts:** orchestrator-agnostic CLI steps (D-020), `fsspec` storage (D-019), provider-agnostic LLM SDK (D-024), city = config file (D-025).

## 5. Miro guide — build it yourself (D-009)
**Time:** about 60–90 minutes, in 4 sittings (zones → boxes → lines → legend). Keep the PNG open on half the screen and Miro on the other.

### 5.0 Setup (5 min)
1. Create a board named **"Saans v1 Architecture"**.
2. Turn on the **grid** and snapping (board settings / view menu) so edges line up.
3. Add a **Frame** (left toolbar → Frame) about **2000 × 1360**. Everything goes inside it, which makes the export clean later.
4. Pick one font for everything (Inter or Open Sans). **Rule:** box titles bold 14–16, details regular 11–12, zone titles bold 18.

### 5.1 Colour kit (copy these hex codes)
| Zone | Fill | Border / accent |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Data sources | `#EEF2FF` | `#6366F1` (indigo) |
| 2 Pipeline | `#ECFDF5` | `#10B981` (green) |
| 3 Storage | `#FFF7ED` | `#F59E0B` (amber) |
| 4 Serving | `#F0F9FF` | `#0EA5E9` (sky) |
| 5 Users | `#FDF2F8` | `#EC4899` (pink) |

- Text: dark `#0F172A`, grey details `#475569`.
- Inner boxes: white fill, border in the zone colour.

### 5.2 Sitting 1: title + five zones (15 min)
1. **Title** (top-left): "Saans — v1 System Architecture (Delhi-NCR)". Grey subtitle: "Hourly batch forecasting · static-first web · grounded AI agent · ₹0/month".
2. Draw **5 tall rounded rectangles**, left to right, all the same height (~990):

| Zone | Approx. x | Width |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Data sources | 30 | 300 |
| 2 Pipeline | 370 | 700 |
| 3 Storage | 1110 | 290 |
| 4 Serving | 1440 | 300 |
| 5 Users | 1780 | 190 |

3. Put the zone title inside each, top-left, in the zone's border colour.
4. **Lock** the five zone rectangles (right-click → Lock) so they don't move while you work inside them.

### 5.3 Sitting 2: boxes (30–40 min)
**Tip:** make one perfect box, then **duplicate** it (Ctrl/Cmd + D) and change the text. Same size, same style, every time.

- **Zone 1:** 7 boxes, 260 × 96, evenly spaced (use the spacing guides Miro shows):
  - CPCB, with a **dashed border** (one-time);
  - OpenAQ;
  - GFS;
  - ADS;
  - CAMS live;
  - FIRMS;
  - City config.
- **Zone 2:**
  - a. Top row: **cron-job.org** (small) → **GitHub Actions** (wide).
  - b. Four **lanes** (white rounded rectangles with a light green border), each with a small green caps label above it: **HOURLY · hourly.yml**, **NIGHTLY · nightly.yml**, **WEEKLY · weekly.yml**, **ON EVERY PUSH · ci.yml**.
  - c. HOURLY lane: **6 equal step boxes** in one row: Ingest, Validate, Features, Forecast, Explain, Publish. Under them, the three grey "Rules / Uncertainty / Never" lines.
  - d. NIGHTLY lane: Evaluate → Scoreboard → Drift report.
  - e. WEEKLY lane: Train → Promotion gate → Register.
  - f. CI lane: three text lines (no boxes).
  - g. Bottom: the **Monitoring** box.
- **Zone 3:** 4 boxes:
  - `<name>-data` (tall);
  - `<name>-live`;
  - `<name>-models`;
  - "Why Hugging Face Hub".
- **Zone 4:** 5 boxes:
  - Web pages;
  - /api/revalidate (short);
  - /api/chat (tall);
  - Upstash Redis;
  - LLM fallback chain.
- **Zone 5:** 2 boxes: Browser / mobile; OpenFreeMap.
- **Optional polish:** a thin coloured **accent bar** on the left edge of each box (a 6-px-wide rectangle in the zone colour). Group it with its box (Ctrl/Cmd + G).

### 5.4 Sitting 3: connectors and number badges (20 min)
Use the **connection line** tool. Drag from a box's edge dot to the target box's edge dot so lines stay attached when boxes move.
- **Style:** dark grey `#334155`, thickness 2, arrow at the end. Use the **elbowed** (right-angle) line type for anything that turns a corner.
- **Dashed** lines for: CPCB backfill, Register → models (weekly), drift alarm → weekly lane.
- **Two-way arrows** for: pipeline ↔ data lake (3), agent ↔ Redis, agent ↔ LLM, users ↔ pages, users ↔ chat.
- **Source bus:** draw one vertical indigo line just right of zone 1, connect each source box to it with a short stub, then **one** thick arrow from the bus into Ingest. This keeps 7 arrows from crossing the whole board.
- **The long ones:**
  - (4) models → up the right edge of zone 2 → into the bottom of Forecast;
  - (6) Publish → down → `<name>-live`;
  - (7) GitHub Actions → **over the top of all zones** → down → /api/revalidate.
- **Number badges:** a 24 × 24 circle, dark fill, white bold number. Place each one **on** its line (duplicate one badge 12 times). Badges 11–12 are pink (users).

### 5.5 Sitting 4: legend + final pass (10 min)
1. A light grey rounded rectangle across the bottom: **Flows 1–12** (copy from §3) in 3 columns, each with its badge.
2. **Line styles:** solid = every hour / request; dashed = one-time, weekly or on alarm.
3. Footer line: "Decisions: D-011 to D-028 in saans/DECISIONS.md".
4. **Final pass:**
   - align everything (select a row → align → distribute evenly);
   - no line crosses a text label;
   - no box overlaps a zone border.

### 5.6 What to send me for review
1. One screenshot of the **whole frame**.
2. One **zoomed** screenshot of zone 2 (the most detailed part).

| R7 | Source bus used (no spaghetti from zone 1) |
| R8 | Pages and agent both read from `<name>-live` (flows 8 and 9), one source of truth |
| R9 | Consistent box sizes, spacing and fonts; nothing overlaps |
| R10 | Readable when the whole frame fits one laptop screen |
| R11 | Legend complete; footer references the decision IDs |
| R12 | Title + subtitle present |
